record.narrative:
All delivered intervals are signed to the registered hypothesis directions and every cell satisfies the minimum-count rule. I used the same clinically meaningful benchmark as in prior appraisals: for outcome_006 and outcome_014, whose absolute mean dependency magnitude is about 0.093, a 10% relative benchmark is about 0.0093; for outcome_005, whose absolute mean magnitude is about 0.25, the benchmark is about 0.025. To support a scientifically meaningful positive association or effect modification, I required the full signed 95% interval to lie beyond the benchmark; mere exclusion of zero was not sufficient, especially given the large number of prior comparisons.

The cross-marker conditional contrasts were not supportive. R193 (H190) tested feature_027 within feature_021=1 for outcome_006; the interval was centered near zero and included effects in both directions. R194 (H191) tested feature_021 within feature_027=1 for outcome_014; although the point estimate was directionally positive, the interval included zero and was compatible with negligible or sub-benchmark effects. Thus these tests did not establish additional outcome-specific marker effects beyond the dominant associations.

The effect-modifier interactions also failed to provide interval-supported evidence of clinically meaningful modification. R195-R196 for high feature_018, R197-R198 for high feature_051, R199-R200 for high feature_043, R201-R202 for high feature_061, and R203 for the outcome_005 feature_021-by-feature_027 interaction all included zero or had intervals compatible with negligible, opposite, or sub-benchmark effects. H196/R199 was the only interval that excluded zero in the positive direction, but its lower bound (+0.0019) was below the outcome_006 benchmark of about +0.0093, so the 95% interval was still compatible with a sub-clinically meaningful modification. I therefore did not accept it as a meaningful interaction.

H168/R204 completed the remaining broad outcome_014 binary screen and was essentially null. Taken together, these results close the final active specificity and modifier checks without adding to the accepted claim set. The supported supplied-dataset landscape remains narrow and outcome-specific: feature_021=1 versus 0 is strongly associated with much higher/less-negative outcome_006, and feature_027=1 versus 0 is strongly associated with much higher/less-negative outcome_014. No independent validation was requested because no new voluntary validation requests remain. These conclusions are dataset-internal and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Iteration 16/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
All newly delivered comparisons are valid independent Welch tests, satisfy the minimum cell-count rule, and are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. I used the same operational clinical benchmark as in prior appraisals: for outcome_006 and outcome_014, whose absolute mean dependency magnitude is about 0.093, a 10% relative benchmark is about 0.0093. To accept a positive association or positive effect modification, I required the full signed 95% interval to lie beyond this benchmark, not merely to exclude zero, because of the large multiplicity of screened comparisons.

The residual marginal screens for feature_046 and feature_001 did not support scientifically meaningful associations. H201/R205 and H203/R207 tested positive feature_046/feature_001 effects on outcome_006; both point estimates were negative and intervals centered near zero with wide negative and positive tails. H202/R206 tested a positive feature_046 effect on outcome_014; the point estimate was positive but the interval included zero and effects below the clinical benchmark. H204/R208 tested a positive feature_001 effect on outcome_014; the point estimate was negative and the interval included zero. These claims are rejected and closed.

The high-percentile modifier screens for feature_021/outcome_006 were also unsupported. H205/R209, H206/R210, H207/R211, and H208/R212 all had intervals including zero and were compatible with null, negative, or sub-benchmark interaction effects. Several of these estimates were negative relative to the registered positive interaction direction. There is no interval-supported evidence that upper-quartile feature_016, feature_053, feature_056, or feature_066 meaningfully amplifies the already accepted feature_021/outcome_006 association.

For the feature_027/outcome_014 interaction screens, H209/R213, H211/R215, and H212/R216 were null or sub-benchmark. H210/R214 is the only result requiring close scrutiny: it nominally excluded zero in the positive direction, with estimate +0.0510 and interval +0.0013 to +0.1007. However, the lower bound is far below the outcome_014 clinical benchmark of about +0.0093, so the interval remains compatible with a sub-clinically meaningful modification. Given the large number of interaction screens, this near-threshold lower bound should not be interpreted as scientifically meaningful effect modification. I therefore reject H210 rather than accepting a clinically significant interaction.

I also noted that several estimates were numerically identical across adjacent modifier screens, especially the feature_016 and feature_066 high-percentile partitions for both outcomes. This likely indicates overlapping partitions, missing-data structure, or highly correlated modifiers rather than independent confirmations. It reinforces treating this batch as one family of related screens and increases the caution warranted against accepting borderline interaction results.

No validation was requested because no voluntary validation requests remain. These conclusions are dataset-internal. They do not establish causality, marker identity, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability. The supported landscape remains the two large, outcome-specific associations already accepted: feature_021 with outcome_006 and feature_027 with outcome_014.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: No response-deadline assessments were due and no new validation evidence was delivered at this synthesis stage; all voluntary validation requests are exhausted. I therefore do not make claim-level reassessments. The supported scientific landscape remains narrow and consists of two strong, outcome-specific, dataset-internal associations. First, feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 is associated with a much less-negative outcome_006 score: accepted main contrast H89/R76 is +0.8019 with discovery interval +0.7823 to +0.8216, and independent validation R79 is +0.7863 with interval +0.7572 to +0.8153. Given outcome_006 mean about -0.093, the 10% operational benchmark is about 0.0093, so these intervals are far above that benchmark. Many accepted stratum-specific contrasts for feature_021/outcome_006 are also around +0.79 to +0.82, e.g. H93/R84, H97/R88, H98/R89, H99/R90, H100/R91, H101/R92, H177/R169, H179/R171, H184/R187, H186/R189, and H188/R191; these are consistency checks rather than independent new claims. Second, feature_027=1 versus feature_027=0 is associated with a much less-negative outcome_014 score: accepted main contrast H39/R38 is +0.7961 with discovery interval +0.7759 to +0.8163, and independent validation R53 is +0.8287 with interval +0.8001 to +0.8574. Accepted stratum-specific contrasts for feature_027/outcome_014, e.g. H94/R85, H95/R86, H96/R87, H178/R170, H180/R172, H185/R188, H187/R190, and H189/R192, are also consistently large and positive. These findings should be interpreted only as dataset-internal associations with weaker measured CRISPR dependency scores; they do not establish causality, mechanism, marker identity, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability. Negative findings are extensive: outside these two associations, no predictor-outcome comparison met the full-interval clinical-benchmark criterion. Weak or borderline nominal results were not accepted when full intervals did not exceed the outcome-specific 10% benchmark, including H73/R75 for feature_052/outcome_006, H107/R99 for feature_021/outcome_005, H113/R105 for feature_021/outcome_016, H160/R164 and H196/R199 for feature_021-by-feature_043 interaction on outcome_006, H173/R185 for feature_007/outcome_006, and H210/R214 for feature_027-by-feature_053 interaction on outcome_014. Several validation results actively refuted weak discovery signals, including H8/R8 versus R13, H15/R15 versus R80, H23/R18 versus R40, H29/R31 versus R39, H31/R22 versus R26, H43/R44 versus R66, H119/R113 versus R120, and H162/R166 versus R168. All tested effect-modification contrasts were incompatible with clinically meaningful modification; the accepted associations were not meaningfully amplified or attenuated by tested binary, categorical, numeric-quantile, or partner-marker modifiers. The feature_021-by-feature_027 interaction was also null. Unresolved uncertainty remains substantial because predictor labels are opaque, validation is within the same supplied dataset, and the very large effects could partly reflect coding artifacts, leakage, latent batch effects, or subtype structure rather than biological dependency relationships. The most informative next analysis is not further isolated screening in this dataset, which would have low expected value and high multiplicity risk, but external replication plus mechanistic perturbation or assay-level inspection of feature_021 with outcome_006 and feature_027 with outcome_014. If only this dataset is available, the best secondary analysis would be a pre-specified joint model over all outcomes and the two dominant markers with interval-based benchmark rules, rather than additional exploratory subgroup comparisons.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The operational clinical benchmark remains 10% of the absolute outcome mean, which is approximately 0.0093 for both outcome_006 and outcome_014. For a positive association or interaction to be accepted, the full signed 95% interval must lie above this benchmark, not merely exclude zero. H225 and H226 are residual marginal screens on outcome_006. Both signed point estimates are negative and both intervals include zero, with upper bounds far below the benchmark; there is no evidence that feature_065 or feature_011=1 versus 0 is associated with a clinically meaningful less-negative outcome_006 score. H227-H231 test whether five numeric modifiers amplify the accepted feature_021/outcome_006 association. Most signed estimates are negative or have intervals spanning zero. Even the largest positive point estimate, H230/R234, has a lower bound compatible with negligible or null interaction and falls below the clinical benchmark when the interval is considered as a whole. H227, H228, H229, and H231 are similarly unsupported and several are incompatible with positive amplification. H232-H236 test effect modification of the accepted feature_027/outcome_014 association. Again, intervals generally include zero or have lower bounds below the benchmark. H233/R237 is the only new comparison with a signed 95% interval excluding zero, estimate approximately +0.0446 and interval approximately +0.0047 to +0.0845. However, its lower bound remains below the clinically meaningful benchmark, and in the context of very large prior multiplicity, especially prior null interaction screens, this nominal positive result is not interval-supported as a clinically meaningful amplification and is plausibly screening noise. Therefore I reject it as a meaningful positive interaction claim. No new scientifically meaningful predictor-outcome association or effect modification is supported. Validation was not requested because no voluntary validation budget remains. The supported dataset-internal landscape remains unchanged and narrow: feature_021=1 versus 0 with less-negative outcome_006, and feature_027=1 versus 0 with less-negative outcome_014. These remain noncausal associations and do not establish marker identity, mechanism, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability. Their implausibly large magnitude also warrants caution about leakage, coding artifacts, latent batch effects, or subtype structure if raw-data inspection were available.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

record.narrative: No response-deadline assessments were due, no new independent validation was delivered, and the voluntary validation budget remains exhausted, so I did not change any accepted or rejected claim or register additional analyses. The final supported dataset-internal evidence is extremely narrow and outcome-specific. First, feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 is associated with a much less-negative outcome_006 CRISPR dependency score, signed discovery estimate +0.8019 with 95% interval +0.7823 to +0.8216 in R76, independently validated at +0.7863 with interval +0.7572 to +0.8153 in R79. Second, feature_027=1 versus feature_027=0 is associated with a much less-negative outcome_014 CRISPR dependency score, signed discovery estimate +0.7961 with interval +0.7759 to +0.8163 in R38, independently validated at +0.8287 with interval +0.8001 to +0.8574 in R53. These effects are far larger than a conservative 10%-of-absolute-mean operational benchmark and are reproduced across many accepted subgroup strata, but they remain associations in the supplied dataset only and do not establish causality, mechanism, predictor identity, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability. All other marginal predictor screens, specificity screens, partner-marker screens, effect-modification screens, and the residual feature_057 high-versus-low tests were not supported at the required interval-benchmark standard; the latest H237-H247 tests were null or below benchmark. Several weak nominal discovery effects also failed independent validation, including examples represented by R13 versus R8, R80 versus R15, R40 versus R18, R39 versus R31, R26 versus R22, R66 versus R44, R120 versus R113, and R168 versus R166. The large outcome_006 association for feature_021 is not mirrored on outcome_014, and the large outcome_014 association for feature_027 is not mirrored on outcome_006, supporting outcome specificity rather than a general dependency shift. The main unresolved issue is scientific validity, not statistical precision: the predictor labels are opaque and the effect sizes are so large that leakage, coding artifacts, deterministic score transformations, clone or batch structure, subtype confounding, or other latent dataset structure are plausible. The most informative next step is external raw-data replication with a pre-specified interval rule and negative-control analyses, together with direct provenance inspection of feature_021 and feature_027; if only the supplied dataset can be used, the best next analysis is an empirical-null calibration or negative-control-outcome audit centered on the two dominant associations, not further ad hoc subgroup mining.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: No claim assessments are due and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted. Given that the only stable dataset-internal signal is dominated by two very large associations, feature_021=1 versus 0 with less-negative outcome_006 and feature_027=1 versus 0 with less-negative outcome_014, the most useful follow-up is not another broad predictor screen. Instead I register focused robustness, heterogeneity, and specificity tests. First, I test whether each accepted association persists in three additional binary strata, feature_007=1, feature_020=1, and feature_012=1, with expected positive direction if the association is not confined to already accepted strata. Second, I test whether feature_011 or feature_005 modifies the accepted associations; direction +1 corresponds to amplification in the named subgroup, but the anticipated direction is null because prior effect-modifier screens have been overwhelmingly null. Third, I test two residual nominal non-dominant-marker signals after removing the dominant marker: feature_007 for outcome_006 among feature_021=0 individuals, and feature_005 for outcome_014 among feature_027=0 individuals. These address whether apparent residual markers are independent associations or are merely artifacts of correlation with the dominant marker. Acceptance will remain conservative: for outcome_006 and outcome_014 I will require the complete signed 95% interval to lie above approximately 0.0093, the 10% absolute-mean operational benchmark, rather than merely excluding zero. These are dataset-internal association tests only and do not support causality, mechanism, predictor identity, therapeutic relevance, or generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: All twelve due tests are valid Welch independent-cell comparisons and were assessed against the same conservative dataset-internal benchmark used in earlier appraisals: for outcome_006 and outcome_014, a positive association was accepted only if the entire signed 95% interval lay above roughly 0.0093, equal to 10% of the absolute outcome mean. H248-H253 decisively meet this standard. Within feature_007=1, feature_020=1, and feature_012=1 strata, feature_021=1 versus 0 remains associated with a much less-negative outcome_006 score, and feature_027=1 versus 0 remains associated with a much less-negative outcome_014 score. The lower bounds are all very far above the benchmark, so although the exposed subgroup cells are smaller, the evidence supports these as dataset-internal persistence/robustness findings. These acceptances are strictly conditional association statements within the supplied dataset; they are not independent validation and do not establish causality, predictor identity, mechanism, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability. The extreme magnitude of both dominant contrasts also leaves leakage, coding artifacts, clone/batch structure, or latent confounding as plausible scientific-validity concerns. record.narrative: No response deadlines were open and no new independent validation was delivered; the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, and no claim status changes are required. The final scientific report is therefore a synthesis of the supplied evidence. The dataset supports a very narrow but very strong set of outcome-specific associations. The first is H89: feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 is associated with a much less-negative outcome_006 dependency score. The signed discovery estimate is +0.8019 with a 95% Welch interval from +0.7823 to +0.8216 in R76, and independent validation gives +0.7863 with a 95% validation interval from +0.7572 to +0.8153 in R79. The second is H39: feature_027=1 versus feature_027=0 is associated with a much less-negative outcome_014 dependency score. The signed discovery estimate is +0.7961 with a 95% Welch interval from +0.7759 to +0.8163 in R38, and independent validation gives +0.8287 with a 95% validation interval from +0.8001 to +0.8574 in R53. Because more negative CRISPR dependency scores denote stronger dependency, these accepted contrasts mean that, within this supplied dataset, the exposed group has weaker measured dependency for the named outcome. Relative to the absolute outcome means of roughly -0.093 for outcome_006 and outcome_014, a 10% absolute-mean benchmark is about 0.0093. The accepted contrasts are far above this benchmark and above any reasonable relative clinical-significance interpretation. Many accepted conditional-stratum claims show persistence of these two lineages across several binary and categorical strata, which supports dataset-internal stability rather than confinement to a single subgroup.   The evidence does not support broad predictors, general dependency shifts, or meaningful effect modification. feature_021 is strongly associated with outcome_006 but not with outcome_014, and feature_027 is strongly associated with outcome_014 but not with outcome_006, supporting outcome specificity. Interaction screens for the two dominant lineages were null or clinically unsupported: feature_027 did not meaningfully modify feature_021 for outcome_006, and feature_021 did not meaningfully modify feature_027 for outcome_014. Numerous other candidate markers, categorical levels, residual conditional markers, median or high-percentile numeric splits, and partner-marker screens were rejected or fell below the interval benchmark. Several nominal discovery findings failed independent validation or did not remain clinically meaningful after validation, including outcome_014 feature_006 with discovery R8 +0.0647 but validation R13 -0.0360; outcome_006 feature_020 with discovery R166 +0.0595 but validation R168 -0.0017; outcome_013 feature_027 with discovery R44 +0.0270 but validation R66 +0.0008; and outcome_006 feature_009 level_003 versus level_001 with discovery R113 +0.0513 but validation R120 +0.0201. These patterns are consistent with multiple-testing noise or small unstable associations rather than supported clinically meaningful effects.   The key remaining uncertainty is scientific validity, not precision. The accepted associations are associations in the supplied dataset only. They do not establish causality, biological mechanism, predictor identity, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability. The effects are unusually large and outcome-specific, and predictor labels are opaque, so leakage, coding artifacts, deterministic score transformations, clone or batch structure, subtype confounding, or dataset-construction artifacts remain plausible. The most informative next analysis is therefore not further ad hoc subgroup mining. It should be a provenance and negative-control audit: inspect the raw generation and coding of feature_021 and feature_027; test whether they predict negative-control or permuted outcomes under an empirical-null calibration; formalize cross-outcome and cross-marker specificity with pre-specified interval rules; and, if an external cohort is available, pre-register and test exactly these two contrasts. If only the supplied dataset is available, a permutation-aware negative-control audit is more informative than additional subgroup screens. The defensible conclusion is: two robust, large, outcome-specific dataset-internal associations are supported, while all other investigated comparisons are unsupported, clinically nonmeaningful, or unvalidated.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

record.narrative: The four new persistence contrasts H260-H263 provide dataset-internal support for the two dominant outcome-specific lineages in additional binary strata. For H260, within feature_011=1, feature_021=1 versus 0 is associated with a much less-negative outcome_006 score: signed estimate +0.8030, lower bound +0.7544, both far above the outcome_006 benchmark of about 0.0093. For H261, within feature_011=1, feature_027=1 versus 0 is associated with a much less-negative outcome_014 score: +0.7895, lower +0.7288, far above the outcome_014 benchmark. H262 and H263 repeat this pattern within feature_005=1, with lower bounds +0.7512 and +0.7183. All cells satisfy the discovery n>=20 rule and the signed interval criterion, so I accept them as conditional association findings in this dataset. I close the specific claims because no further subgroup mining is scientifically useful without independent validation or provenance information. The four residual-marker audits do not establish independent secondary effects. H264 is near zero and crosses zero. H265 has a point estimate of +0.0424 for feature_020 within feature_021=1, but its lower bound +0.0003 is below the clinical benchmark, so it cannot be accepted as a robust clinically meaningful residual association. H266 and H267 are opposite-signed near zero and cross zero. The outcome-specificity tests H268-H271 are unsupported: feature_021 does not show interval-supported clinical effects on outcome_005, outcome_013, or outcome_008 under the tested conditioning, and feature_027 does not show an interval-supported clinical effect on outcome_005 under the tested conditioning. All intervals cross zero or fall below the relevant 10%-absolute-mean benchmark. No validation request is made because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted. The accepted persistence findings remain dataset-internal associations only; leakage, coding artifacts, clone/batch structure, latent confounding, or predictor-label identity remain unresolved scientific-validity concerns.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

This is the final scientific synthesis. The dataset supports two large, outcome-specific, interval-supported associations and their dataset-internal conditional-persistence strata. For outcome_006, H89 accepts that feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 is associated with a much less-negative dependency score: R76 signed discovery estimate +0.8019 with 95% Welch interval +0.7823 to +0.8216; R79 independent validation estimate +0.7863 with interval +0.7572 to +0.8153. For outcome_014, H39 accepts that feature_027=1 versus feature_027=0 is associated with a much less-negative dependency score: R38 signed discovery estimate +0.7961 with interval +0.7759 to +0.8163; R53 validation estimate +0.8287 with interval +0.8001 to +0.8574. Because more negative scores mean stronger dependency, these accepted contrasts mean weaker measured dependency in the exposed group for the named outcome. Using the absolute outcome means near -0.093, the conservative 10%-absolute-mean benchmark is about 0.0093; the accepted lower bounds are far above this benchmark and far exceed a 10% meaningfulness threshold. The same pattern persists across many dataset-internal conditional strata, including H93, H95, H97 through H101, H177 through H189, H248 through H253, and H260 through H263, supporting internal stability but not external generality. The evidence does not support broad or general dependency shifts. feature_021 does not show an interval-supported clinically meaningful association with outcome_014, and feature_027 does not with outcome_006. Many other predictors, categorical levels, numeric splits, residual markers, and interaction screens are rejected because intervals cross zero or do not lie wholly above the relevant absolute-mean benchmark. Examples: H264 through H267 fail residual-marker audits; H268 through H271 fail outcome-specificity tests. Several nominal discovery findings also failed independent validation, for example H8 outcome_014 feature_006 with discovery R8 +0.0647 but validation R13 -0.0360; H164 outcome_006 feature_020 with discovery R166 +0.0595 but validation R168 -0.0017; H43 outcome_013 feature_027 with discovery R44 +0.0270 but validation R66 +0.0008; and H119 outcome_006 feature_009 level_003 versus level_001 with discovery R113 +0.0513 but validation R120 +0.0201. These patterns support multiple-testing noise or unstable small associations rather than supported clinically meaningful effects. The main unresolved issue is validity and interpretation, not precision. The accepted associations are dataset-internal only; they do not establish that feature_021 or feature_027 cause dependency changes, identify their biological meaning, or generalize outside this dataset. Their enormous size and outcome specificity, together with opaque predictor labels, make leakage, deterministic coding, clone or batch or subtype artifacts, or predictor-to-outcome construction overlap plausible. The most informative next analysis is therefore not more subgroup mining. It should be a provenance and negative-control audit of feature_021 and feature_027: inspect generation and coding and possible overlap with outcome_006 and outcome_014; test exact or near-exact prediction; run empirical-null or permutation calibration against permuted or negative-control outcomes; perform a pre-specified cross-outcome and cross-marker specificity matrix; and, if available, pre-register exactly these two contrasts for external replication. The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

This is the final scientific synthesis. The dataset supports two large, outcome-specific, interval-supported associations and their dataset-internal conditional-persistence strata. For outcome_006, H89 accepts that feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 is associated with a much less-negative dependency score: R76 signed discovery estimate +0.8019 with 95% Welch interval +0.7823 to +0.8216; R79 independent validation estimate +0.7863 with interval +0.7572 to +0.8153. For outcome_014, H39 accepts that feature_027=1 versus feature_027=0 is associated with a much less-negative dependency score: R38 signed discovery estimate +0.7961 with interval +0.7759 to +0.8163; R53 validation estimate +0.8287 with interval +0.8001 to +0.8574. Because more negative scores mean stronger dependency, these accepted contrasts mean weaker measured dependency in the exposed group for the named outcome. Using the absolute outcome means near -0.093, the conservative 10%-absolute-mean benchmark is about 0.0093; the accepted lower bounds are far above this benchmark and far exceed a 10% meaningfulness threshold. The same pattern persists across many dataset-internal conditional strata, including H93, H95, H97 through H101, H177 through H189, H248 through H253, and H260 through H263, supporting internal stability but not external generality. The evidence does not support broad or general dependency shifts. feature_021 does not show an interval-supported clinically meaningful association with outcome_014, and feature_027 does not with outcome_006. Many other predictors, categorical levels, numeric splits, residual markers, and interaction screens are rejected because intervals cross zero or do not lie wholly above the relevant absolute-mean benchmark. Examples: H264 through H267 fail residual-marker audits; H268 through H271 fail outcome-specificity tests. Several nominal discovery findings also failed independent validation, for example H8 outcome_014 feature_006 with discovery R8 +0.0647 but validation R13 -0.0360; H164 outcome_006 feature_020 with discovery R166 +0.0595 but validation R168 -0.0017; H43 outcome_013 feature_027 with discovery R44 +0.0270 but validation R66 +0.0008; and H119 outcome_006 feature_009 level_003 versus level_001 with discovery R113 +0.0513 but validation R120 +0.0201. These patterns support multiple-testing noise or unstable small associations rather than supported clinically meaningful effects. The main unresolved issue is validity and interpretation, not precision. The accepted associations are dataset-internal only; they do not establish that feature_021 or feature_027 cause dependency changes, identify their biological meaning, or generalize outside this dataset. The absolute mean of outcome_001 is about 0.4155, so the dataset-internal 10%-absolute-mean benchmark is about 0.0415. For each signed positive hypothesis, I will accept only if the entire 95% Welch interval lies above this benchmark and all comparison cells satisfy the discovery minimum.
